correctness.rationale: In coordinates s=x+y, t=z+w, a=x−y, b=z−w the quartic is s^4+t^4=a^4+b^4 and C=(s²+t²−a²−b²)/4. Swapping s,t without swapping a,b is a projective automorphism preserving A,B,C. The independent swap and the signed permutations of a,b form a faithful order-16 group H. This equals the degree of the finite map from the base-point-free quadrics because (2H_X)^2=16, proving Galoisness. G is the index-two kernel of the product of the two swap signs. Z=(s+t)(s−t)(b²−a²) is G-invariant and squares to the branch form; on A≠0 the weight-zero generator is Z/A² and its square has odd valuation along A=0. The reduced branch has precisely five normal crossings by the conic determinant and line restrictions. The resulting double plane is a normal finite model of the fixed field, with completed local equations z²=uv at the five crossings and no further singularities. The branch line bundle O(2) gives anticanonical pullback O(1), whose three sections are precisely those from the plane by the double-cover pushforward. The five Du Val points give the asserted crepant resolution. The independent expansion and fixed-locus checks agree with the surviving original theorem.
residual_risks: The group is the full coordinate-permutation group in the original coordinates, not the full group of projective or abstract automorphisms. The symbolic replay independently checks identities and crossings; normality, Galoisness and the canonical bundle use the proof.
